elements.name: A1_T1
elements.html: Please spend a few minutes exploring the tool before beginning the survey. Click the icon in your browser toolbar near the top-right corner of the browser window. Be sure to view all parts of the interface.

elements.name: A1_Q1
elements.title: Briefly describe (1-2 sentences), what do you think is the purpose of this tool?

elements.name: A1_Q2
elements.title: Please list the new information, if any, you learned by using this tool.

elements.title: Please list the information you already knew, if any, that the tool told you.

elements.name: A1_Q4

elements.name: A2_T1
elements.html: Next we would like to understand your thoughts, awareness, and comfort around Google Activity data after using our designed personalised dashboard (ADA) for a week.

elements.name: A2_Q1
elements.title: Compared to before your weeklong usage of ADA, how would you describe your overall awareness of what Google stores about your activity?

elements.name: A2_T2
elements.html:
Please rate your agreement with each statement below, grouped into three areas:

System Quality
Ease of Use & Interaction Experience
Perceived Usefulness

On a scale of 1 to 5, where 1 indicates “Strongly disagree” and 5 indicates “Strongly agree.”

elements.name: A2_Q2
elements.title: System Quality (Data, Recommendations & Clarity)

rows.text: The activity information shown in ADA regarding my activities felt accurate.
The activity information shown in ADA regarding my activities felt reliable.
The activity information provided by the extension matches my idea of how sensitive my browser interactions are.
I understand why ADA marked certain entries as more sensitive than the others.

elements.name: A2_Q3
elements.title: Ease of Use & Interaction Experience

rows.text: The extension is easy to navigate.
The extension is easy to interact with.
The activity information provided by the extension is easy for me to understand.
The order in which the recommendations are presented by the browser is easy for me to understand.
The extension was overall presented in a way that was easy for me to understand.

elements.name: A2_Q4
elements.title: Perceived Usefulness

rows.text: ADA helped me understand the potential 'sensitivity' of my data quickly.
ADA helped me notice things about my Google activity that I was not aware of before.
Using this extension would help me better manage my browsing data.
Using this extension would improve to remove sensitive data from being shipped to google.
I would be open to using this extension in my day-to-day life.
I trust the personalized dashboard provided by the system.
The personalized dashboard helps me decide which activities to delete.

elements.name: A2_Q5
elements.title: Privacy & Trust

rows.text: I trust that ADA handled all my data privately on my device.
Knowing my data never left my device made me feel safe using ADA.

elements.name: AC_2
elements.title: Please select "Disagree" for this statement so that we know you are reading carefully.

elements.name: A2_Q6
elements.title: How did you feel using ADA by the end of the 7-day period?

elements.name: A2_T3
elements.html:
Over the past week, ADA ranked and re-ordered your activity items. Thinking about how the tool ordered your activity items — please rate your agreement with each statement below, grouped into three areas:

Agreement
Stability
Trust and responsiveness

Answer choices for all questions in this section: Strongly agree · Agree · Neither agree nor disagree · Disagree · Strongly disagree

elements.name: A2_Q7
elements.title: Agreement

rows.text: The items the tool put at the top were the ones I also consider most sensitive.
The tool's ordering of the activity items reflected what matters to me personally.
The tool's ordering of the activity items seemed like it would be the same for anyone.

elements.name: A2_Q8
elements.title: Stability

rows.text: The tool's ordering of the activity items stayed consistent over the week.
When the ordering of the activity items changed, the changes made sense to me.
The ordering of the activity items changed more often than I would have liked.

elements.name: A2_Q9
elements.title: Trust and responsiveness

rows.text: The tool seemed to adjust to me (became more personalised) over the course of the week.
I could predict how the tool would treat a new item of my activity.

elements.name: A2_Q10
elements.title: Did you notice the tool's ordering change at any point during the week?

elements.name: A2_Q10_B1
elements.title: In your own words, what changed, and what did you make of it?

elements.name: A5_Q1
elements.title: Compared to before you used the tool, how likely are you to do each of the following now?

rows.text: Seek out more information about how companies store your activity
Review your Google activity history
Delete items from your activity history
Turn off or pause an Activity Control
Set your activity to auto-delete after a fixed period
Use Incognito mode or browse signed out

elements.name: A6_Q1
elements.title: For each pair below, imagine you had to choose between Option A and Option B. Please indicate which you would choose.

rows.text: A: Free access to services, but your activity is stored indefinitely. B: A monthly fee, but no activity is stored.
A: Your activity is deleted automatically after three months, but recommendations get worse. B: Your activity is kept forever, and recommendations stay accurate.
A: Your search results are not personalized, but nothing you search is stored. B: Your results are personalized, but everything you search is stored.
A: A company decides which of your activity is sensitive. B: You label which of your activity is sensitive yourself, but must do it manually.

pages.name: A7
pages.title: Opinions about Activity Collection and Personalization

elements.name: A3_T1
elements.html: The following section repeats some of the questions you answered in the pre-usage part of this study. This is intentional: we would like to understand whether, and how, your opinions may have changed after using ADA for the past week. As before, during the rest of this survey, we use the term 'activity data' to refer to the records a company (e.g., Google) keeps of what you searched for, watched, visited, or did while using its services.

elements.name: A7_Q1
elements.title: Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with each of the following statements.

rows.text: I would like the services I use to be personalized based on my past activity, as opposed to being the same for everyone.
I would be comfortable with a company keeping a record of what I search for and watch.
If it were available, I would like to use a system that shows me what activity data has been collected about me.
I feel that companies adequately explain what they keep in my activity history.
I feel that I understand how companies decide what to keep in my activity history.
I would consider it fair for a company to store my activity in order to personalize the services I use.
I would consider it creepy for a company to store my activity in order to personalize the services I use.
